title: Identifying the end user in model calls (end-user IDs)

videos.script: Every call Tarefa makes to its model provider goes out on one API key. Thousands of people, one name. {{title}} So when one of them misbehaves, the provider sees Tarefa misbehaving. And Tarefa's own logs can say which account, but only if somebody wrote it down. {{one-key}} An end-user ID fixes both. It is a short string sent with each call, saying which of your users this is. {{id}} It must not be the person's e-mail. And a plain hash of the e-mail is not much better. The lab undoes one in two hundred and fifty-seven guesses. {{reverse}} A keyed hash cannot be undone that way, and a different key for each provider keeps two providers from joining their records. {{hmac}} Then the ID does a second job, at home. One user runs a script, and with a single limit on the key, all six users lose requests. {{flood}} With a limit per user as well, only the script is refused. {{per-user}}
